criteria.text: Diagnosis of insomnia with sleep onset and/or maintenance difficulty
Patient is at least 18 years old
Other physical or psychiatric causes of sleep disturbance have been ruled out
Medication-induced sleep disturbance considered and addressed as clinically appropriate
Documented trial and failure of two prescription sleep aids
Documented trial of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT)
CBT included education on sleep hygiene improvements
CBT included counseling on common misconceptions about sleep/insomnia
Denial if: Patient has a narcolepsy diagnosis
Denial if: Patient is taking another sedative hypnotic agent concurrently

notes: Partial encoding of archived Alaska Medicaid Orexin Receptor Antagonists criteria, effective 2022-06-01. Belsomra (suvorexant), Dayvigo (lemborexant), and Quviviq (daridorexant) share all approval and denial criteria. Failure to meet approval criteria is a denial.

Clinical documentation and trial/failure facts are attestations; evidence verification requires manual review. Medication adjustments must minimize effects on sleep, for example earlier dosing or decreased dosage, as clinically appropriate.

Cautions (notes only): May impair alertness and motor coordination, including morning impairment; may worsen depression or suicidal ideation; complex sleep behaviors including sleep-walking, sleep-driving, or other activities while not fully awake; sleep paralysis, hypnagogic/hypnopompic hallucinations, and cataplexy-like symptoms may occur.
Duration (notes only): initial approval up to 3 months; reauthorization up to 6 months.

Quantity (notes only): Belsomra 30 tablets per 30 days, all strengths (5mg, 10mg, 15mg, 20mg); Dayvigo 30 tablets per 30 days, all strengths (5mg, 10mg); Quviviq 30 tablets per 30 days, all strengths (25mg, 50mg). max_units is null. Cautions, duration, reauthorization and quantity enforcement require manual review. PDL status unknown; no linked alternatives.
